q: Which of the following Indus Valley sites is famous for its ancient dockyard?
exp: Lothal (located in Gujarat near the Bhogava river) had a massive brick-lined dockyard used for maritime trade.

q: The 'Great Bath' of the Indus Valley Civilization was discovered at:
exp: The Great Bath, a large public water tank likely used for ritual bathing, was excavated at Mohenjodaro.

q: The famous 'Gayatri Mantra' is found in which Mandala of the Rig Veda?
exp: The Gayatri Mantra, dedicated to Savitri, is composed by Vishwamitra and appears in the 3rd Mandala of the Rig Veda.

q: Where did Gautama Buddha deliver his first sermon (Dharmachakrapravartana)?
exp: Buddha delivered his first sermon to five ascetics at the Deer Park (Isipatana) in Sarnath, near Varanasi.

q: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kashmir under the patronage of which ruler?
exp: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held at Kundalvana in Kashmir under Kushan emperor Kanishka, presided over by Vasumitra.

q: Who deciphered the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts of Ashokan inscriptions in 1837?
exp: James Prinsep, an officer of the East India Company mint, deciphered the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts in 1837.

q: Which Ashokan Rock Edict describes the horrors of the Kalinga War and Ashoka's remorse?
exp: Major Rock Edict XIII records Ashoka's victory over Kalinga and his subsequent turn towards Dhamma.

q: Megasthenes, the Greek ambassador who wrote 'Indica', visited the court of:
exp: Megasthenes was sent by Seleucus I Nicator as an ambassador to the Mauryan court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra.

q: The 'Prayag Prashasti' (Allahabad Pillar Inscription) celebrating Samudragupta's conquests was composed by:
exp: Harishena, the court poet and minister of Samudragupta, composed the Prayag Prashasti in classical Sanskrit.

q: The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Fa-Hien (Faxian) visited India during the reign of:
exp: Fa-Hien visited India between 399 and 414 CE during the reign of Gupta emperor Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).

q: The Aihole Inscription, which records the defeat of Harshavardhana by Pulakeshin II, was composed by:
exp: Ravikirti, the Jain court poet of Chalukya king Pulakeshin II, composed the Aihole Prashasti.

q: The famous Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur was built by which Chola ruler?
exp: Rajaraja Chola I completed the Brihadeeswarar Temple (Rajarajeshwaram) in 1010 CE; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: The Chola local self-government (village assemblies like Sabha and Ur) is famously detailed in the inscriptions of:
exp: The Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I provide detailed rules for the election and functioning of village committees (Variyams).

q: Who among the following Delhi Sultans introduced the market control policy and the 'Dagh' (branding of horses) system?
exp: Alauddin Khalji introduced strict market price regulations, Dagh (horse branding), and Chehra (descriptive roll of soldiers).

q: The 'Iqta' system of land revenue assignment was institutionalized in the Delhi Sultanate by:
exp: Shams-ud-din Iltutmish institutionalized the Iqta system, dividing the empire into tracts assigned to officers (Iqtadars) in lieu of salary.

q: The Moroccan traveler Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of which Delhi Sultan?
exp: Ibn Battuta arrived in India in 1333 CE during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign and was appointed Qazi of Delhi.

q: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 CE on the banks of the Tungabhadra river by:
opts: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I
exp: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I of the Sangama dynasty founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 CE.

q: Who authored the famous Telugu work 'Amuktamalyada'?
exp: Vijayanagara emperor Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva dynasty) authored Amuktamalyada in Telugu and Jambavati Kalyanam in Sanskrit.

q: The First Battle of Panipat (1526), which established Mughal rule in India, was fought between Babur and:
exp: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat in April 1526 using artillery and the Tulughma tactic.

q: The 'Dahsala' (Zabti) land revenue system under Emperor Akbar was formulated by:
exp: Raja Todar Mal introduced the Ain-i-Dahsala system in 1580, fixing revenue based on the average produce and prices of the preceding ten years.

q: In the Mughal Mansabdari system, what did the terms 'Zat' and 'Sawar' denote respectively?
opts: Personal rank/salary and number of cavalrymen to maintain
exp: 'Zat' fixed the personal status and salary of a Mansabdar, while 'Sawar' indicated the number of cavalrymen he was required to maintain.

q: Who among the following Bhakti saints was a disciple of Ramananda and composed verses included in the Guru Granth Sahib?
exp: Kabir, a Nirguna Bhakti saint and disciple of Ramananda, criticized ritualism; many of his verses are preserved in the Guru Granth Sahib.

q: The Treaty of Purandar (1665) was signed between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and:
exp: The Treaty of Purandar was signed on 11 June 1665 between Shivaji and Mughal commander Mirza Raja Jai Singh I.

q: In the Battle of Plassey (1757), the British East India Company forces were led by:
